hazards: Manual handling of shell/panels
Two-plus person lift or hoist for shell; use body cart/rotisserie once landed.
Shell on stands — stability
Confirm stands/fixture rated for shell weight before releasing hoist.
qc: Within tolerance at all checked points
None, or documented/claimed before work begins
steps: Uncrate and inspect the new Dynacorn reproduction shell for shipping damage, panel alignment and e-coat/paint condition.
No teardown required — shell arrives as new sheet metal, not a restored body.
Mount shell on rotisserie or chassis fixture; confirm level and square before any structural work begins.
Dimensionally check core body points — shock tower centres, front rail width, rear frame rail length — against the Dynacorn spec sheet.
⚠ Confirm dimensions before OP-201 — the parcel shelf brace and Front IFS install both depend on an accurate shell.
Photograph shell condition and record any shipping damage claims before proceeding.

diagramCaption: Original schematic — parcel shelf brace location & rear seatbelt anchor points (not to scale; reflex angle fits to body per Step 2)
materials: Parcel shelf assembly — supplied part, P/N: [enter part number]
hazards: Cutting / grinding sparks
Clear flammables from bay; fire extinguisher within reach.
Welding fumes / arc flash
Ventilated bay; welding mask and gauntlets.
steps: Receive and inspect the parcel shelf assembly (P/N: [enter part number]) against the reference drawing — confirm mounting hole layout, ADR harness cut-outs and panel condition before fitting.
✔ This is a supplied part, not fabricated on-site — check it against the drawing for shipping damage or defect, don't re-cut it.
parcel_shelf_drawing.jpg
Parcel shelf drawing — supplied part reference, P/N: [enter part number]
Dry-fit the parcel shelf panel across the rear package tray, confirming it seats against the body's reflex angle and rear seat bulkhead.
⚠ Reflex angle is body-specific — confirm the fold/seat angle against the actual shell in this fixture; no fixed spec is issued for this yet, fit to the body.
Clamp the panel in place and tack weld the parcel shelf brace to the body structure at the marked points.
Confirm fitment and structural alignment before final weld — check for panel oil-canning or gaps against the body.
✔ No gaps or high spots before proceeding to final weld.
Fully weld the parcel shelf brace to the body seam per structural weld standard.
✔ Continuous weld bead, no gaps, cold-lap or pinholes.

title: ADR-Compliant Seatbelt Mounting Plate Upgrade
next: OP-010 — Front K-Member, Shock Tower Saddle & Frame Rail Preparation (Section 03).
materials: ADR-compliant seatbelt mounting plate kit (interim upgrade)
Note: this operation may be removed from the standard travel sheet if/when Dynacorn supplies ADR-compliant seatbelt mounting as standard equipment.
hazards: Cutting / grinding sparks
Clear flammables from bay; fire extinguisher within reach.
Welding fumes / arc flash
Ventilated bay; welding mask and gauntlets.
steps: Locate factory seatbelt anchor points and confirm against the ADR seatbelt anchorage design rule.
Remove or reinforce any factory mounting points that don't meet the compliant spec.
Fit and weld ADR-compliant seatbelt mounting plates at the lower anchor, upper anchor (B-pillar) and inertia reel positions — tie rear mounts into the parcel shelf brace from OP-201.
✔ Rear belt loads route through the parcel shelf brace, not bare sheet metal.
Confirm all mounting plate welds and drill any clearance holes required for belt hardware.

title: Front K-Member, Shock Tower Saddle & Frame Rail Preparation (Section 03).
next: OP-020 — Shock Tower Saddle Fit-Up & Tack Weld.
hazards: Vehicle on jack stands / hoist
Stands on flat frame-rail sections near front body mounts only; confirm vehicle stability before working underneath.
Cutting / grinding sparks
Clear flammables from bay; fire extinguisher within reach; eye and hand protection mandatory.
Welding fumes / arc flash
Local extraction or open bay ventilation; welding mask and gauntlets; screen off adjacent stations.
Suspended engine/component during removal
Use rated hoist/engine crane; no body parts under suspended load.
qc: Frame rails cleaned to bare metal in weld zone
All removed fasteners tagged and retained
Shock tower cut lines clean, on apron edge
steps: Raise vehicle and support on jack stands placed on the flat section of the frame rails, close to the front body mounts.
⚠ Confirm stand placement before releasing hoist. Vehicle must not rock.
Remove engine and transmission. Tag and bag all fasteners for re-installation.
✔ Every fastener labelled by location — zero loose/unlabelled fasteners at end of step.
Remove front wheels and shocks. Disconnect brake lines and tie rods.
Cap open brake lines to prevent fluid loss / contamination.
Remove the factory steering box, pitman arm, and lower control arms. Unbolt the factory crossmember from the frame. Cut out the factory lower control arm mounts.
Reference cut lines only where marked — do not cut into the main frame rail.
p03_f0.jpg
Fig. 1 — cut-out control arm mounts
Cut out the factory shock towers, cutting along the edge between the shock tower and the inner apron for a clean line — passenger side.
✔ Clean, straight cut on the apron edge — this becomes the weld joint for the new inner fender panel.
p04_f0.jpg
Fig. 2 — passenger side
Cut out the factory shock tower — driver's side.
✔ Match passenger side cut line.
p04_f1.jpg
Fig. 3 — driver's side, tower removed
Grind and clean the remaining front frame rails — top, bottom, inner and outer faces — down to bare, weld-ready metal.
✔ No paint, rust, or coating within the weld zone.
p04_f2.jpg
Fig. 4 — bottom view of engine bay
Measure 24-1/4" from the very front of the frame and mark a vertical Sharpie line on each rail — passenger side shown.
⚠ CRITICAL DIMENSION — re-check measurement on both sides before marking.
p05_f0.jpg
Fig. 5 — spindle centreline mark
Repeat the 24-1/4" centreline mark — driver's side.
Error here affects final wheel alignment.
p05_f1.jpg
Fig. 6 — driver's side, 24 1/4"

title: Shock Tower Saddle Fit-Up & Tack Weld
next: OP-030 — K-Member Installation & Final Weld.
materials: Factory 7/16" steering gear bolt (alignment tool only)
Factory 3/8" idler arm bolt (alignment tool only)
hazards: Vehicle on jack stands / hoist
Stands on flat frame-rail sections near front body mounts only; confirm vehicle stability before working underneath.
Welding fumes / arc flash (tack weld)
Welding mask and gauntlets; ventilated bay.
Sharp cut edges on frame rail
Deburr edges or wear cut-resistant gloves when handling.
qc: Spindle centreline visible through saddle slot, both sides
Saddle orientation — front hole higher than rear
Saddles clamped snug, no gap to frame rail
steps: Place the driver's side shock tower saddle onto the frame rail. Orient so the upper control arm mount hole is higher at the front than the rear.
Confirm orientation before clamping — front hole higher than rear.
Use the factory 7/16" steering gear bolt to pre-locate the driver's side saddle, sliding it through the front ½" hole in the saddle and the ½" factory frame rail hole.
Factory bolt is an alignment guide only — discard once saddle is aligned.
p07_f0.jpg
Fig. 7A — driver's side alignment bolt
Use the factory 3/8" idler arm bolt to pre-locate the passenger's side saddle through the rear ½" hole in the saddle and the rear ½" hole in the frame rail.
Discard factory bolt once aligned.
p07_f1.jpg
Fig. 7B — passenger side alignment bolt
Check the slot in each shock tower saddle against the spindle centreline mark made in OP-010. The vertical Sharpie line must be visible through the slot.
⚠ Do not proceed until the centreline mark is visible through the slot on both sides.
p06_f0.jpg
Fig. 7 — saddle alignment window
Use adjustable clamps to securely snug both shock tower saddles to the frame rails, then tack weld in place.
✔ Tack only — full weld occurs in OP-030 after K-member fit-up.
p06_f1.jpg
Fig. 8 — clamped for tack weld

title: K-Member Installation & Final Weld
next: OP-040 — Lower Ball Joint & Lower Control Arm Installation.
materials: HEIDTS front K-member sub-frame (motor stands pre-welded on)
hazards: Vehicle on jack stands / hoist
Stands on flat frame-rail sections near front body mounts only; confirm vehicle stability before working underneath.
K-member weight during fit-up
Support with engine crane or transmission jack while positioning; do not hand-hold under load.
Full-seam welding — fumes, arc flash, burns
Ventilation, welding mask/gauntlets, screen adjacent stations, allow cool-down before handling.
qc: K-member slots aligned to saddle slots
Full weld — no gaps, pinholes or cold-lap
steps: Place the front K-member into the vehicle, locating the vertical slots on the K-member to the vertical slots of the saddles. Use adjustable clamps to secure the K-member to the frame rail saddles and rear frame rails.
Slots must align — do not force; re-check saddle position if binding.
p08_f0.jpg
Fig. 9 — align slots at spindle centreline
Confirm the motor stands (pre-welded to the K-member) are correctly oriented before welding.
✔ Re-check spindle centreline alignment before welding — last point to correct it.
p09_f0.jpg
Fig. 10 — motor stands, driver's side
Fully weld all seams and slots between the K-member and the vehicle frame — driver's side, view from outside vehicle.
✔ Continuous weld bead, no gaps or cold-lap.
p10_f0.jpg
Fig. 11 — driver's side, outside view
Complete the weld — driver's side, view from engine compartment.
Grind smooth per your finishing standard.
p10_f1.jpg
Fig. 13 — driver's side, engine bay view

title: Lower Ball Joint & Lower Control Arm Installation
next: OP-050 — Upper Control Arm, Ball Joint & Caster/Camber Slug Installation.
hazards: Vehicle on jack stands / hoist
Stands on flat frame-rail sections near front body mounts only; confirm vehicle stability before working underneath.
Thread damage from cross-threading ball joint
Start by hand, use anti-seize, do not force.
qc: Ball joint threads coated with anti-seize before install
Correct bolt length used front vs rear (4½" vs 5")
Ball joint boot seated on top side
steps: Apply anti-seize to the threads of the lower screw-in ball joint.
✔ Anti-seize on every ball joint thread before install — no exceptions.
p11_f0.jpg
Fig. 14 — ball joint, anti-seize
Install the lower ball joint into the control arm housing. Tighten until tight to the housing.
Confirm ball joint seats fully — no gap to housing.
p11_f1.jpg
Fig. 15 — ball joint housing
Place the ball joint boot on the top side of the housing.
Boot orientation matters — top side only, or it will not seal correctly.
p11_f2.jpg
Fig. 16 — boot installed

Install the lower control arms. Use 5/8-11 x 4½" hex bolts, washers and Nylock nuts for the front mount; 5/8-11 x 5" hex bolts, washers and Nylock nuts for the rear mount. The cut-out on the bottom of the cross member is for the front bolt.
Torque per fastener spec sheet — do not fully torque until ride height is set, unless your procedure specifies otherwise.
p12_f0.jpg
Fig. 17/18 — control arm + cross-member cut-out
Confirm final control arm position and fastening.
Verify against fastener spec.
p12_f1.jpg
Fig. 19 — control arm installed

title: Upper Control Arm, Ball Joint & Caster/Camber Slug Installation
next: OP-060 — Steering Arm & Spindle Installation.
materials: Aluminium upper control arm slugs — 0" offset (base kit, 4 supplied)
Moog K960 camber shim kit (optional, if adjusting beyond base setting)
hazards: Vehicle on jack stands / hoist
Stands on flat frame-rail sections near front body mounts only; confirm vehicle stability before working underneath.
qc: Correct slug offset installed both sides (match unless deliberate correction)
Upper control arm bolts torqued to spec
steps: Install the upper control arm ball joints.
p13_f0.jpg
Fig. 20A — upper ball joint installed
Install the aluminium upper control arm slugs into the upper control arm slotted shaft for desired caster. Base kit ships with 0" offset slugs (measured from bolt centre), giving 4–5° of caster.
If more caster is required, source offset slugs (1/16" increments, Lefthander Chassis) rather than modifying the base slugs.
p13_f1.jpg
Fig. 21A — LHC upper control arm slugs
Reference: available slug offset options if a non-zero setting is needed.
Record offset used per side for the alignment log.
p14_f0.jpg
Fig. 21B — slug offset options
If adjusting camber beyond the base setting, add camber shim plates between the shock tower and the outside of the upper control arm shaft (Moog K960 kit).
Record shim thickness used per side for the alignment record in OP-100.
p14_f1.jpg
Fig. 21C — Moog K960 camber shims
Secure the upper control arm with the supplied ½-20 x 2¾" Grade 8 hex bolts.
Torque per fastener spec sheet.
p15_f0.jpg
Fig. 21D — upper control arm assembled

title: Steering Arm & Spindle Installation
next: OP-070 — Coilover Shock Installation.
materials: Castle nuts + cotter pins (lower/upper ball joint retention)
hazards: Vehicle on jack stands / hoist
Stands on flat frame-rail sections near front body mounts only; confirm vehicle stability before working underneath.
Red thread locker — skin/eye contact
Wear gloves; avoid contact with skin and eyes.
qc: Steering arms oriented forward, both sides
Thread locker present on all steering arm fasteners
Cotter pins fitted, new, both ball joints, both sides
steps: Apply red thread locker to all steering arm fastener threads before installation.
✔ Thread locker on every steering arm fastener — steering-critical joint.
p15_f1.jpg
Fig. 22 — thread locker on bolt
Install the steering arms to the spindles.
Confirm steering arms face forward before final torque.
p15_f2.jpg
Fig. 23 — steering arm
Install the spindle over the lower ball joint first. Thread the castle nut over the washer to secure the spindle to the lower ball joint.
p16_f0.jpg
Fig. 24 — steering arms face forward
Attach the upper ball joint to the spindle.
Confirm orientation matches Fig. 24 reference.
p16_f1.jpg
Fig. 25 — spindle attached to ball joints
Torque castle nuts to spec and fit new cotter pins through both upper and lower ball joints.
⚠ Steering-critical fastener — do not reuse cotter pins. Advance torque (never back off) to align the slot.
p17_f0.jpg
Fig. 26 — castle nut installed

title: Coilover Shock Installation
next: OP-080 — Sway Bar Installation.
materials: 6× ½-20 x 2¾" Grade 8 Hex Bolt (lower mount)
2× ½-20 x 5" Grade 8 Hex Bolt (upper mount)
hazards: Vehicle on jack stands / hoist
Stands on flat frame-rail sections near front body mounts only; confirm vehicle stability before working underneath.
Spring under compression (coilover)
Handle assembled coilovers with care; do not disassemble spring/shock without a spring compressor.
qc: Shock spacers fitted at upper mount, both sides
Upper and lower mount bolts torqued to spec
steps: Install the coil-over shocks. Use ½-20 x 2¾" Grade 8 hex bolts, washers and Nylock nuts for the lower control arm mount.
p17_f1.jpg
Fig. 27 — coilover installed
Confirm the adjuster knob faces in-board for ease of adjustment.
⚠ Adjuster orientation — in-board on both sides, or later adjustment access is blocked by the frame.
p17_f2.jpg
Fig. 28 — adjuster knob orientation
Use ½-20 x 5" Grade 8 hex bolts, washers and Nylock nuts along with the aluminium shock spacers (MTF-216) to secure the shock to the upper mount.
Torque per fastener spec sheet.
p18_f0.jpg
Fig. 29 — upper shock mount
Confirm final coilover position and fastening.
Verify spacer count — 4 total across both sides.
p18_f1.jpg
Fig. 30 — upper mount detail

title: Sway Bar Installation
next: OP-090 — Rack & Pinion Installation.
materials: 7/16-14 x 1½" Grade 8 bolts, washers, Nylock nuts
hazards: Vehicle on jack stands / hoist
Stands on flat frame-rail sections near front body mounts only; confirm vehicle stability before working underneath.
Tack/final weld of sway bar mounting brackets
Welding mask, ventilation, screen adjacent stations.
qc: End links straight (vertical) both axes, both sides
Mounting bracket flush to bottom of frame before tack
Full weld on mounting brackets, no gaps
Sway bar collars tightened, bar centred
steps: Attach the sway bar to the adjustable end links and mount the end links snug to the lower control arm mounts. Confirm end links sit straight up and down, front-to-rear and left-to-right. Apply anti-seize to adjustable link threads.
Mount the female rod end on the top side to avoid trapping water in the threads.
p18_f2.jpg
Fig. 31/32 — end link assembly

Install the sway bar bushings using 7/16-14 x 1½" Grade 8 bolts, washers and Nylock nuts, with 3/8" spacers, to the sway bar mounting brackets. Clamp the assembly to the factory frame — driver's side shown.
Re-check end link bushings are still straight up and down before tacking.
p19_f0.jpg
Fig. 33 — driver's side, clamped
Once the mounting bracket is flush with the bottom of the frame, tack weld the mounting bracket to the frame.
p19_f1.jpg
Fig. 34 — mounting bracket tacked
Install and tighten the sway bar collars. Once the sway bar is at the desired location, fully weld the sway bar mounting brackets to the frame.
✔ Full weld only after collar position confirmed correct — rework after full weld is difficult.
p19_f3.jpg
Fig. 35 — collar installed
Grease the bushings and install the splined sway bar and torsion arm, confirming the adjustable link is straight up and down, front-to-rear and right-to-left — full underside view.
p20_f0.jpg
Fig. 36 — full assembly, underside
Confirm bushing and clamping collar seating from inside the sway bar mount.
Passenger side shown — mirror for driver's side.
p20_f1.jpg
Fig. 37 — bushing & collar detail
Confirm splined sway bar final position, passenger side.
p21_f0.jpg
Fig. 38 — splined sway bar, passenger side

title: Rack & Pinion Installation
next: OP-100 — Ride Height, Alignment & Road Test.
tools: Socket head cap screw driver / Allen key set
hazards: Vehicle on jack stands / hoist
Stands on flat frame-rail sections near front body mounts only; confirm vehicle stability before working underneath.
qc: Rack & pinion mount bolts torqued to spec, all 4
Outer tie rods connected both sides, boots undamaged
steps: Install the billet rack mount brackets on top of the rack mount tabs. Remove the billet rack mount caps and position the rack and pinion in place.
Use the four socket head cap screw bolts to fasten the rack & pinion and rack mounts to the cross member. Attach the outer tie rod to the steering arm.
Torque per fastener spec sheet. Confirm tie rod boot is not twisted or pinched before final torque.
p21_f1.jpg
Fig. 39/40 — rack & pinion installed

title: Ride Height, Alignment & Road Test
next: End of front IFS installation sequence — proceed to next chassis station per build travel sheet.
materials: Camber shim plates (Moog K960 or equivalent, as required)
hazards: Vehicle on jack stands / hoist
Stands on flat frame-rail sections near front body mounts only; confirm vehicle stability before working underneath.
Road test of unproven suspension build
Low-speed shakedown first; check for noise, binding or looseness before normal driving.
steps: Set the vehicle at final ride height with the lower control arms level before setting alignment.
⚠ Alignment must be set at ride height, not on the hoist with suspension drooped.
Set caster using the upper control arm mount slugs installed in OP-050. Zero-offset slugs should fall within the recommended caster window.
Target: 3° to 6° positive caster.
Set camber by adding or subtracting camber shim plates at the upper control arm.
Target: 0° to 2° negative camber.
Set toe.
Target: 0 to 1/16" toe-in.
Confirm both sides have equal caster settings.
⚠ Unequal caster side-to-side will cause the vehicle to pull — do not release for road test until matched.
Road test for a few hundred miles, then re-check ride height and alignment. Springs may settle and change ride height/camber — re-adjust ride height before re-checking alignment.
Schedule a follow-up alignment check post-settling before final customer/compliance sign-off.

title: Rear Axle, 4-Link / Torque Arm & Panhard Bar Mounting
next: OP-402 — Rear Coilover / Spring & Parking Brake Cable Routing.
hazards: Vehicle on jack stands / hoist
Stands on flat frame-rail sections near front body mounts only; confirm vehicle stability before working underneath.
Suspended axle assembly
Support on rated stands/jack; no body parts under suspended load.
Welding fumes / arc flash
Ventilated bay; welding mask and gauntlets.
steps: Position rear axle assembly under the vehicle at correct ride height and pinion angle.
Fit 4-link/torque arm brackets and Panhard/Watts link mount, confirming axle centreline against chassis centreline.
⚠ CRITICAL — axle centreline must match chassis centreline before any welding.
Tack weld all mounting brackets; verify axle is square before final weld.
Fully weld all mounting brackets to the frame.
✔ Continuous weld bead, no gaps.

title: Rear Coilover / Spring & Parking Brake Cable Routing
next: OP-501 — Brake Line Fabrication & Master Cylinder / Booster Install.
hazards: Spring under compression
Handle assembled coilovers with care; use a spring compressor if disassembling.
steps: Install rear coilovers/springs and shocks per kit instructions; confirm ride height.
Route parking brake cables clear of exhaust, driveshaft and moving suspension components.
✔ Check clearance through full suspension travel, not just static.
Torque all suspension fasteners to spec.

title: Brake Line Fabrication & Master Cylinder / Booster Install
next: OP-502 — Fuel Cell / Tank Install, Fuel Lines & Brake Bleed.
hazards: Brake fluid — skin/eye/paint contact
Wear gloves and glasses; wipe spills immediately, brake fluid damages paint.
qc: No contact with moving or hot components
Torqued to spec, no weeping under pressure test
steps: Install master cylinder, booster (if fitted) and proportioning valve.
Fabricate and route brake lines front to rear, securing with mounting clips at factory intervals.
No line within 50mm of exhaust or moving suspension without a heat shield/clearance check.
Connect lines to calipers/wheel cylinders; torque all fittings to spec.

title: Fuel Cell / Tank Install, Fuel Lines & Brake Bleed
next: OP-601 — Engine & Transmission Install.
hazards: Fuel vapour — fire risk
No open flame or grinding nearby; ensure bay ventilation.
Pressurised brake bleed
Wear eye protection; relieve pressure before disconnecting.
steps: Install fuel cell/tank and mounting straps; connect fuel supply/return lines and vent per fuel system diagram.
Pressure/leak-test fuel system before first start.
⚠ Do not proceed to OP-601 first start until fuel system passes leak test.
Bench or manual bleed the complete brake system; verify pedal feel and no leaks.

title: Engine & Transmission Install
next: OP-602 — Driveshaft Fit, Exhaust Fabrication & Cooling System.
hazards: Vehicle on jack stands / hoist
Stands on flat frame-rail sections near front body mounts only; confirm vehicle stability before working underneath.
Suspended engine/transmission load
Use rated hoist/crane; no body parts under suspended load.
steps: Lower engine/transmission assembly onto mounts; confirm mount alignment and clearance to chassis/body.
Connect engine mounts, transmission crossmember and driveline accessories.
Torque all mounting hardware to spec.
✔ Re-check torque after first heat cycle.

title: Driveshaft Fit & Exhaust Fabrication
next: OP-603 — Engine Bay Ancillary Components (Radiator, Brake Booster & Electric Pump Brackets).
hazards: Cutting/welding exhaust — sparks, fumes
Ventilated bay; fire extinguisher within reach.
qc: Clears all lines/floor by minimum margin
steps: Fit driveshaft; confirm u-joint angles and slip-yoke engagement.
Fabricate and install exhaust system, maintaining clearance from fuel lines, brake lines and floor.
Minimum clearance per your fabrication standard — check at full suspension travel.

title: Engine Bay Ancillary Components — Radiator, Brake Booster & Electric Pump Brackets
next: OP-604 — Engine Bay Plumbing (Brake, A/C & Coolant Line Routing).
hazards: Manual handling / sharp bracket edges
Deburr fabricated brackets; wear gloves when fitting.
qc: Electric MC pump bracket — passenger side
Clear of wheel/suspension through full travel
Electric A/C pump bracket — driver side
Clear of wheel/suspension through full travel
steps: Install radiator and confirm clearance to fan, core support and A/C condenser.
Install brake booster / master cylinder assembly at the firewall.
Fabricate and fit the mounting bracket for the electric master cylinder pump under the front fender, passenger side.
✔ Confirm bracket location matches this build's standard — passenger side, under-fender.
Fabricate and fit the mounting bracket for the electric A/C pump under the front fender, driver side.
✔ Confirm bracket location matches this build's standard — driver side, under-fender.
Confirm clearance to wheel, tyre and suspension travel for both fender-mounted pump brackets through full lock and full suspension travel.
⚠ Check at full steering lock and full bump/droop — not just static.

title: Engine Bay Plumbing — Brake, A/C & Coolant Line Routing
next: OP-701 — Chassis Harness Install.
hazards: Brake fluid — skin/eye/paint contact
Wear gloves and glasses; wipe spills immediately.
Refrigerant handling (A/C charging)
Only charge A/C with certified equipment and refrigerant handling licence.
qc: No chafe points through full steering/suspension travel
steps: Run brake lines from the electric master cylinder pump (passenger fender) to the booster/master cylinder and forward to the front brake circuit fabricated in OP-501.
Run A/C lines from the electric A/C pump (driver fender) to the compressor/condenser circuit.
Route coolant hoses between radiator and engine, clear of exhaust and moving components.
Secure all lines with mounting clips at factory-style intervals; confirm no chafe points through full steering and suspension travel.
⚠ Check at full steering lock and full suspension travel, both fender pump lines included.

title: Chassis Harness Install
next: OP-702 — Engine Harness, ECU Integration & Gauge/Switch Wiring.
hazards: Battery — short circuit / arc risk
Disconnect battery before harness work; insulate loose terminals.
